newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dragonair plans new Hong Kong-China routes.
newsitem.headline: Dragonair plans new Hong Kong-China routes.

text.p: Hong Kong Dragon Airlines (Dragonair) is to launch its 16th regional service to mainland China with an inaugural flight to Chongqing on April 23, senior airline officials said.

Following the handing back of Hong Kong to China at midnight on June 30, the China-controlled regional carrier is also studying additional HK-China routes including Wuhan, Fuzhou and Shantou, said Augustus Tang, the airline's planning and international affairs general manager.
"We hope to go Wuhan this year because it has been top of our wanted list for some time," Tang said.
Dragonair said Chongqing on the Yangtse River is its second destination in fast-growing Sichuan province along with Chengdu.
It said it sees the potential for rapid growth from both business and leisure passenger traffic. The 168-seat Airbus A320 service will initially be twice weekly on Wednesday and Sundays.
Dragonair is also hoping to increase its twice-weekly frequency to Phnom Penh in Cambodia and has already announced that it is planning to boost services to Japan, including a new service to Niigata.
Pusan has been a long held ambition but "bogged down" traffic rights negotiations have so far precluded the carrier's first South Korean destination, the airline said.
Dragonair currently flies to 25 destinations across the region.
It is to take delivery of its fifth Airbus A330 in June with three more aircraft due to arrive in the next two years to capitalise on the opening of Hong Kong's new airport at Chek Lap Kok.
Currently constrained by slot restrictions at its current home base, Kai Tak airport, Tang said he expects to have a 15 aircraft fleet of A320s and A330s by 1999.

"We are very positive about the future. Chek Lap Kok will open up new opportunities for us with new routes and additional frequencies, allowing us more convenient scheduling and improved aircraft rotation," he said.

"We shall be looking to new routes and additional frequencies in China after July the first. Everything is in place to capatalise on future opportunities after July when Hong Kong becomes part of China again," Tang added.
